title: applied-ml-weekly-notes-2026-04-14
content:
Weekly applied-ml notes - 2026-04-14

Attendees: Priya, Ethan, Diego, Maya, Sophie (remote)
Meeting length: 45m

High-level status
- Focus this week: quantization experiments for Llama2-13B / RedModel-7B, evaluation harness stabilization, and onboarding checklist for new open-model variants.
- Overall: experiments progressing, some quality regressions with aggressive int8 profiles, eval infra flaky on long-context tests.

Standup updates (quick bullets)
- Priya: ran int8 PTQ sweep on Llama2-13B with 4 different calibration sets; latency down ~2.3x on p4d-8x with current runtime kernels, but LM perplexity increased by ~6-9% depending on profile. Collecting sample generations for manual triage. Open PR for instrumentation to log token-level logits for failure cases - PR #842 linked above.
- Ethan: updated eval harness to support dynamic context length sampling; found a bug in batching that caused occasional context truncation for >8192 tokens. Patch submitted, tests added. Working on stable metric aggregation across seeds.
- Diego: kernel selection tuning - implemented heuristic to prefer tiled attention kernel when sequence<1024 and model quantized. Early results: 8-12% latency improvement for short requests. Seeing memory fragmentation in long-lived pods - investigating leak.
- Maya: onboarding two community models (RedModel-7B and OpenChat-4B). Completed tokenizer sanity checks for RedModel-7B; building quantized artifacts. Need decisions on default safety prompts for OpenChat-4B.
- Sophie: running end-to-end regression eval against Canary traffic subset. Noted a small but visible safety regression in a single prompt cluster after int8 conversion - keeping that subset for focused manual eval.

Research notes - Quantization
- Experiments run this week:
  - Llama2-13B: FP16 baseline vs int8 PTQ (symmetric vs per-channel) vs mixed FP16+int8 on attention weights. Calibration sets: random-wiki-10k, convai-dialogues-3k, internal-prod-sample-1k.
  - RedModel-7B: Q4_0 simulated profile via quantize-tool v0.9.

- Observations:
  - Latency: int8 PTQ gives 2x-2.5x throughput improvement on p4d when batching is moderate (batch size 4-8). Mixed FP16+int8 beneficial for tail latency.
  - Quality: average perplexity increases: symmetric int8 ~9%, per-channel int8 ~5%, mixed FP16+int8 ~3%. For prompt-sensitive categories (code-gen, math) regressions are larger.
  - Failure modes: occasional tokenization mismatch when using custom tokenizer merges + quantized embeddings - likely due to rounding in embedding projection. Need to add deterministic post-calibration checks.
  - Stability: PTQ with small calibration sets (1k) shows higher variance. Recommendation: use >=3k diverse calibration samples for production profiles.

- Next experiments planned:
  - Run QAT-lite for RedModel-7B on a few thousand steps to see if regresses close. Estimate 48-72h GPU time.
  - Add per-layer activation range logging during calibration to detect outlier layers.
  - Validate mixed precision kernel selection in runtime for both throughput and correctness at scale.

Evals
- Harness updates:
  - Fixed batching truncation bug (Ethan). Re-ran earlier regressions for 2026-04-01 checkpoints.
  - Added resource-limited synthetic workload to simulate 95th percentile tail.

- Results summary:
  - Canary run against int8 Llama2-13B: generation quality (ROUGE-L / BLEU analogs) down 2-4% on average, but certain clusters (technical writing, math) down 8-12%.
  - Safety checks: minor uptick in hallucination scoring on product-qa cluster for one profile. Keeping that profile out of canary until further triage.

Model onboarding notes
- RedModel-7B:
  - Tokenizer: passed special token checks, vocab mapping consistent with our tokenizer wrapper.
  - Weights: converted to internal format, ran single-node FP16 smoke test - memory profile good.
  - Quant artifacts: building Q4_0 and per-channel int8. Need to produce a small eval report for product that shows perf vs cost tradeoffs.
- OpenChat-4B:
  - Safety prompt decision needed from product - default to conservative safety prompts until product approves.
  - Integration: function-calling tests pending.

Operational notes
- Logging: added token-level logits capture flag (opt-in) for debugging quantization failures. Flag is off by default; will enable for failing canary subset only.
- Monitoring: added histograms for per-request kernel selection and quant profile used. Will add alert for profile churn > 10% day-over-day.

Blockers / Risks
- Memory fragmentation in runtime when switching kernels frequently - Diego investigating, may require allocator rewrite.
- Eval flakiness on long-context stress tests - could delay rollout of int8 profiles for models used with long contexts.
- Product decision pending on safety prompt for OpenChat-4B - blocks onboarding to hosted catalog.

Action items (owners + due dates)
- Priya: Collate sample generations for Llama2-13B int8 regressions and post to channel for manual triage - due 2026-04-16.
- Ethan: Merge batching-fix and deploy eval harness to canary infra - due 2026-04-15.
- Diego: Debug memory fragmentation & propose mitigation (short term: pod restart heuristic; long term: allocator fix) - status update 2026-04-17.
- Maya: Finish RedModel-7B eval report (perf/cost/quality) and draft product-facing onboarding doc - due 2026-04-20.
- Sophie: Run focused safety regressions on the preserved prompt cluster and enumerate failing prompts - due 2026-04-16.

Notes to self / loose thoughts
- Consider adding a small synthetic calibration set per customer to reduce variance of PTQ when customers bring custom vocab.
- Try a hybrid calibration strategy: large generic calibration + small customer-specific delta.
- Need to formalize QA gating for quantized model promotion into Dedicated vs Hosted tiers.

Links and artifacts (again)
- PR: serving-runtime PR #842 - instrumentation and token-logging.
- JIRA: JIRA-ML-573 - quantization experiment tracking.
- Confluence: quantization experiment pages - sketch of calibration heuristics.

Next meeting: 2026-04-21 10:30 PT

End of notes.
